svg.aria-label: Two panels. Traditional architecture: clients reach a load balancer, which spreads requests across application servers that all read and write one database, so the database is on the request path and becomes the bottleneck. Space-based architecture: clients reach a messaging grid, which routes requests to processing units that each hold application logic and an in-memory data grid; the units feed data pumps, which update the database asynchronously, so the database is off the request path
svg.text: Space-based architecture serves requests from memory and moves the database off the request path.
All writes go to the database.
Database becomes the bottleneck under high traffic.
Limited by connections, lock contention, and write throughput.
Adding more application servers does not solve database limits.
Reads and writes are served from in-memory data grids.
Database is updated asynchronously via data pumps.
Scales elastically by adding more processing units.
Handles high write contention and traffic spikes.
Database is on the request path.
Data is kept in memory and the database is off the request path.
